title: Design System: FH-MUM NJF Hotel Accommodation Planner

display.purpose: Hotel totals, the pull tally and the pull screen heading. Narrow bold.

headline.purpose: Page-bar title, section headings and side-panel titles. Narrow bold.

title.purpose: Hotel names in the summary, settings and message-day headings. Normal width.

table.purpose: Table cells, list rows and notices; buttons, tabs and field labels at weight 600.

label.purpose: Buttons, tabs, section links and field labels.

caption.purpose: Table headers, notes, counts and chart axes. The smallest size allowed.

tag.purpose: Tour numbers on tags and stay bars. Narrow bold, line-height 1.

mono.purpose: Hotel message text as it will be pasted, and inline codes.

tagHues.source: assignHues() in src/lib/tags.ts gives each pulled tour one hue; tours whose dates overlap do not share a hue while hues remain. useHue() sets it as --h on the element.

shadows.name: side-panel
shadows.purpose: The drawer over the scrim. The only overlay shadow.

shadows.name: segment-selected
shadows.purpose: The raised pill of the pressed option in a segmented control.

shadows.name: stay-bar-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover feedback on a clickable stay bar.

shadows.name: field-focus
shadows.purpose: Focus ring on inputs and selects, with a rail border.

shadows.name: focus-outline
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on everything else; white on the rail.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The one easing curve (--ease), for reveals, chevrons and the side panel.

motion.name: state-colour
motion.purpose: Background, border and text colour on hover, press and selection.

motion.name: chevron
motion.purpose: Disclosure chevrons turning; also the scrim fade.

motion.name: night-reveal
motion.purpose: A night row opening in place (fade with a top-down clip).

motion.name: side-panel
motion.purpose: The drawer sliding in from the right.

motion.name: pull-day
motion.purpose: A day cell filling as the pull reads it.

motion.name: count-up
motion.purpose: A total counting to its new value.

motion.name: saving-pulse
motion.purpose: The rail status dot while edits are saving.

motion.name: active-step-ring
motion.purpose: The current step while a pull is running.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Loops, reveals, slides and count-ups stop; colour changes stay.

narrative.overview:
The look comes from the colour-coded lanyards and luggage tags a ziyarat group carries. Every tour is a tag: a tinted pill with a punched hole and bold narrow lettering. The plan is read by following a tag's colour across the changes list, the nightly tables, the rooms-by-night board, the room picker and the hotel messages. The owner chose this direction; it replaced the previous look entirely.

The page is bright and flat: white surfaces on a faintly blue canvas, one ultramarine rail across the top, and thin lines instead of shadows. It is a working tool (surface mode: Operate) used mostly on a laptop or desktop, so density is high and the first screen is the plan itself: summary line, NKERP changes, then the occupancy chart. It does not open on a row of same-size stat cards or a dark splash.
keyCharacteristics: One strong colour for the frame (the rail); colour elsewhere always means a tour, a hotel or a state.
Twelve tag hues, one per tour, the same on every screen.
Three hotel data colours in the order the hotels fill: teal, amber, raspberry.
One type family in two widths; six sizes; tabular numerals everywhere.
Flat tonal layering; shadows only on the side panel and as state feedback.
Colour transitions only. Movement is limited to panels, disclosures and the pull progress.

rules.name: The Tag Follows the Tour Rule
rules.body: Hues are assigned once, from every tour pulled for either city (`assignHues` in `src/lib/tags.ts`), and read with `useHue()`, so a tour has one colour on every tab. Tours whose dates overlap do not share a hue while hues remain. Never assign a tag colour by position, hotel or status.

rules.name: The Hotels Are Data Rule
rules.body: Hotel colours mark hotels only; tag colours mark tours only. They share hues, so form separates them: a tag is a pill with a punched hole, a hotel is a square dot, a flat chip or a chart fill.

rules.name: The Blue Changed, Red Problem Rule
rules.body: Blue wash means NKERP changed it. Red means the plan cannot work as it stands. Nothing else uses either.

rules.name: The Neutral Caution Rule
rules.body: A caution is a white notice with an orange icon, never an amber fill, so it cannot be read as the amber hotel.

rules.name: The Six Sizes Rule
rules.body: Type uses `--fs-1` to `--fs-6` (0.75, 0.8125, 0.875, 1, 1.25, 1.75rem). Nothing is set below 0.75rem (12px).

rules.name: The Two Widths Rule
rules.body: Narrow bold is for headings, tags and numerals that are read as figures. Sentences stay at normal width.

rules.name: The Header Under the Bar Rule
rules.body: Above 1180px every table header and the room board's date row stick directly under the page bar (`top: var(--bar-h)`); inside a side panel they stick to the panel top.

rules.name: The Notes Stay On Screen Rule
rules.body: Warnings and NKERP changes live in the row's Notes column. The groups table uses a fixed layout so that column fits without sideways scrolling at desktop width; on a phone the note spans the full card.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: A shadow is a response to state or an overlay. Panels are separated by lines and tone.

dos: Do put a tour tag wherever a tour appears, coloured through `useHue()`.
Do list and stack hotels in fill order: Ruya, Araf, Hotel C.
Do add a colour as an OKLCH token on `:root` before using it.
Do put a warning in the row's Notes cell, next to the control that fixes it.
Do keep every control at least 24px tall, and 44px on touch.
Do give each page bar a single primary button.
Do say in the rail whether edits are saved.
donts: Don't open a screen on a row of same-size stat cards or a dark splash; the plan comes first.
Don't use a hotel colour for a tour, a status or a warning, or a tag colour for a hotel.
Don't use blue wash for anything except "changed in NKERP", or red for anything except a problem.
Don't fill a caution with amber or yellow.
Don't add a seventh type size or set text below 12px.
Don't add resting shadows to cards, or motion that is not a state change.
Don't invent a logo, photography or brand marks; none exist.
